newsitem.title: USA: PageNet sees growth in cash flow.
newsitem.headline: PageNet sees growth in cash flow.

text.p: Paging Network Inc said Tuesday it sees its growing domestic cash flow continuing to exceed capital expenditures in future quarters.

"While the timing of capital expenditures may cause results to vary quarter to quarter, we expect our core domestic operating cash flow to continue to exceed the capital required for that business in subsequent quarters," said Glenn Marschel, president and chief executive.

"We expect continued growth in operating cash flow and improving operating cash flow margins in the core domestic business," he said. "We are on track to achieve core operating cash flow in excess of capital expenditures and interest associated with that business in 1998."
The company said its aim is to keep its leverage ratio below 5.5 times for the remainder of 1997 and in 1998, barring unforeseen business events.
The company today reported a second quarter net loss of $0.49 per share, including an extraordinary charge of $0.15, compared with a net loss of $0.18 a year earlier.

During the quarter the company added 538,149 pagers to service, including 109,380 alphanumeric and 2,474 VoiceNow pagers. Pagers in service at the end of the quarter totalled 10,057,941, a 27.6 percent increase over 7,881,764 at the end of the second quarter of 1996, the company said.
The company's monthly churn rate in its domestic direct channel for the second quarter was 2.0 percent, compared to 2.4 percent in the second quarter of 1996.
The rate is the lowest in the company's history.
Second quarter operating cash flow totaled $78.9 million, a 22.2 percent increase over the $64.6 million for the second quarter of 1996.
Operating cash flow margins for the core domestic paging business were 38.7 percent in the second quarter of, compared to 37.5 percent a year earlier.
